hints: Look closely at the charge on the $\text{XO}_4^{2-}$ ion, it tells you the oxidation number that X must be able to reach.
Work out the oxidation number of X in $\text{XO}_4^{2-}$ and check whether phosphorus or sulfur can show that oxidation state in Period 3.
For Y, write the balanced equations for sodium and magnesium with chlorine and see which one uses Y and $\text{Cl}_2$ in an exact 1 to 1 mole ratio.
walkthrough:
**Find the oxidation number of X in XO4 2-**

Think of the ion as a little maths puzzle. Oxygen is almost always -2.

Let oxidation number of X be x:
$$x + 4(-2) = -2$$
$$x - 8 = -2$$
$$x = +6$$
So element X must be able to form a +6 oxidation state in its oxide and acid.

**Decide between phosphorus and sulfur**

Now remember your Period 3 maximum oxidation numbers. They equal the group number.

Phosphorus is in Group 15, so its maximum is +5, as in $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ and $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$. Sulfur is in Group 16, so its maximum is +6, as in $\text{SO}_3$ and $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$.

Only sulfur can give $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$. The chemistry is:
$$\text{SO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$$
which ionises to give $2\text{H}^+ + \text{SO}_4^{2-}$. So X is sulfur.

**Use the reacting moles to identify Y**

Write the two possible equations with chlorine, $\text{Cl}_2$:
$$2\text{Na} + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NaCl}$$
$$\text{Mg} + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{MgCl}_2$$
For sodium, 1 mol of Na needs only 0.5 mol of $\text{Cl}_2$. For magnesium, 1 mol of Mg needs exactly 1 mol of $\text{Cl}_2$.

The question says 1 mol Y reacts exactly with 1 mol $\text{Cl}_2$ with nothing left over. That matches magnesium only. So Y is magnesium.

options.A: Incorrect. Phosphorus cannot reach +6, its maximum is +5, so it forms $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$ not $\text{XO}_4^{2-}$. Sodium is also wrong because $2\text{Na} + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NaCl}$ needs a 2 to 1 ratio, not 1 to 1.
options.B: Half right, half wrong. Magnesium is correct for Y because $\text{Mg} + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{MgCl}_2$ is 1 to 1, but phosphorus is wrong for X because it cannot form a +6 $\text{XO}_4^{2-}$ ion.
options.C: Half right, half wrong. Sulfur is correct for X because it forms $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ with S in +6, but sodium is wrong for Y because 1 mol Na would leave half of the 1 mol $\text{Cl}_2$ unreacted.
options.D: Correct and well done. X is sulfur because only S(VI) gives $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$, and Y is magnesium because only $\text{Mg} + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{MgCl}_2$ uses exactly 1 mol of metal with 1 mol of chlorine molecules.
